name: E-commerce
tagline: Orders, customers, products, returns and fulfilment for online stores
description: Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and custom-store exports, including Indian-market fields such as COD, RTO, GST, PIN code and courier.

fields.label: Order ID
fields.description: Identifies each online order; repeats on every line of a multi-item order. An invoice, bill or receipt number is the shop's or seller's billing key, not the order.

fields.label: AWB / tracking number
fields.description: The courier's air waybill or tracking number for the parcel: a sign of goods shipped to the buyer.

fields.label: Shipping method
fields.description: The delivery service the buyer chose at checkout (standard, express, same day).

fields.label: Fulfilment channel
fields.description: Who packed and shipped the order: the marketplace (FBA, Flipkart Smart) or the seller.

fields.label: COD flag
fields.description: Marks cash-on-delivery orders (1 or yes), the rest being prepaid.

fields.label: Delivery days
fields.description: Days from order to delivery as the export already counts them (a delivery TAT column).

fields.label: New customer flag
fields.description: Marks a customer's first order with the store, as online stores record it (yes or no).

subDomains.name: Orders & transactions
subDomains.description: One row per order or order line.

subDomains.name: Returns & refunds
subDomains.description: One row per return or refund.

subDomains.name: Customer master
subDomains.description: One row per customer with lifetime totals.

subDomains.name: Product catalogue
subDomains.description: One row per SKU with price and cost.

subDomains.name: Ad / marketing performance
subDomains.description: Spend and results per campaign and day.

kpis.name: Gross sales (GMV)
kpis.definition: Total value of everything ordered, before discounts, cancellations and returns.
kpis.formula: Sum of line gross value (quantity × unit selling price) across all orders

variants.label: Net amount (no gross available)
variants.caveat: No gross, price or discount column, so GMV equals net sales here.

pitfalls: GMV is not revenue: it includes orders that are later cancelled, returned or RTO'd.

kpis.name: Discounts
kpis.definition: Value given away through coupons and markdowns.

variants.label: Gross minus net
variants.caveat: Derived as gross minus net, so it also includes any other deductions.

variants.label: Quantity × unit price × discount %
variants.caveat: No discount amount column, so discounts are rebuilt from quantity, unit price and the line discount %.

kpis.name: Net sales (all orders)
kpis.definition: Value after discounts across every order placed, including those later cancelled or returned.

variants.label: Gross (no discounts recorded)
variants.caveat: No discount column, so net sales equal gross sales.

kpis.name: Net revenue
kpis.definition: Revenue actually kept: net of discounts and excluding cancelled, returned and RTO orders.
kpis.formula: Net sales on orders that were not cancelled, returned or RTO

variants.label: Excludes cancelled / returned / RTO by status
Net sales (no status column)
variants.caveat: No status, return flag or refund column, so cancelled and returned orders are still included.

pitfalls: Recent days look low until in-transit orders are delivered or returned; compare complete periods.

kpis.name: Orders
kpis.definition: Number of distinct orders placed.

variants.label: Row count (no order ID)
variants.caveat: No order ID column, so every row is counted as one order. Check the grain.

kpis.name: Realised orders
kpis.definition: Orders not cancelled, returned or RTO'd.
kpis.formula: Distinct order IDs excluding cancelled, returned and RTO statuses

kpis.name: Average order value
kpis.definition: Net revenue earned per realised order.
kpis.formula: Net revenue ÷ realised orders (ratio of sums, not an average of order values)

variants.label: Net revenue ÷ orders
variants.caveat: No status column, so the denominator includes cancelled orders.

pitfalls: A rising AOV can come from fewer small orders rather than bigger baskets; check orders alongside.

kpis.name: Units ordered
kpis.definition: Total items ordered.

kpis.name: Items per order
kpis.definition: Average basket size in units.

kpis.name: Average selling price
kpis.definition: Net sales per unit sold, weighted by quantity.

kpis.name: Discount %
kpis.definition: Share of gross sales given away as discounts.
pitfalls: Averaging line-level discount % overweights cheap items; this KPI is a ratio of sums.

kpis.name: Coupon usage rate
kpis.definition: Share of orders that used a coupon code.

kpis.name: Coupon AOV uplift
kpis.definition: How much larger (or smaller) coupon orders are than orders without a coupon.
kpis.formula: AOV with coupon ÷ AOV without coupon − 1
pitfalls: Coupon users self-select (e.g. larger planned baskets to hit a threshold); uplift is correlation, not causation.

kpis.name: Shipping cost %
kpis.definition: Logistics cost as a share of net revenue.

kpis.name: COGS (all orders)
kpis.definition: Cost of goods across all order lines.

kpis.name: Cost of goods sold
kpis.definition: Cost of the goods on realised orders.
kpis.formula: Line cost on orders not cancelled, returned or RTO

kpis.name: Gross profit
kpis.definition: Net revenue minus cost of goods sold.

kpis.name: Gross margin %
kpis.definition: Share of net revenue left after the cost of goods.

benchmark.note: Indicative range for D2C brands; varies widely by category.

kpis.name: Cancellation rate
kpis.definition: Share of orders cancelled before fulfilment.

benchmark.note: Indicative; COD orders usually cancel more often than prepaid.

kpis.name: RTO rate
kpis.definition: Share of shipped orders that came back to the seller undelivered (return to origin).

benchmark.note: Indicative range for Indian D2C; COD-heavy categories sit at the top.

pitfalls: The denominator excludes cancelled orders, which never shipped.

kpis.name: Returned orders
kpis.definition: Orders the customer sent back after delivery.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct orders with a returned status

kpis.name: Return rate
kpis.definition: Share of delivered orders that customers returned.

variants.label: Returned ÷ shipped orders
variants.caveat: No delivered status found, so in-transit orders are in the denominator; recent periods understate returns.

variants.label: Returned flag ÷ orders
variants.caveat: No status column, so cancelled orders are in the denominator.

benchmark.note: Fashion and footwear commonly see 15–30%; electronics and beauty are lower.

kpis.name: Refund rate (value)
kpis.definition: Refunded value as a share of gross sales.

kpis.name: Average delivery time
kpis.definition: Calendar days from order to delivery, for delivered orders.
kpis.formula: Average of (delivery date − order date) in days

variants.label: Delivery-days column
variants.caveat: No delivery date, so the file's own delivery-days column is averaged.

pitfalls: Multi-line orders count once per line; heavy multi-item orders weigh more.

kpis.name: Time to dispatch
kpis.definition: Calendar days from order to shipment.
kpis.formula: Average of (ship date − order date) in days

kpis.name: COD share
kpis.definition: Share of orders paid by cash on delivery.

variants.label: COD-flagged orders ÷ orders
variants.caveat: No payment-method column, so the COD flag column is used.

pitfalls: A high COD share raises RTO risk and delays cash collection.

kpis.name: RTO rate — COD
kpis.definition: RTO rate on cash-on-delivery orders.
kpis.formula: RTO rate filtered to COD orders

kpis.name: RTO rate — prepaid
kpis.definition: RTO rate on prepaid orders.
kpis.formula: RTO rate filtered to non-COD orders

kpis.name: COD cancellation rate
kpis.definition: Cancellation rate on cash-on-delivery orders.
kpis.formula: Cancellation rate filtered to COD orders

kpis.name: Customers
kpis.definition: Distinct customers who ordered in the period.

kpis.name: New customers
kpis.definition: Customers whose first-ever order falls in the period.
kpis.formula: Customers with first order date ≥ period start
pitfalls: Customers whose first order predates this file look new. The longer the history, the more accurate this is.

kpis.name: Returning customers
kpis.definition: Customers who ordered in the period and had ordered before.

kpis.name: Returning customer share
kpis.definition: Share of the period's customers who had ordered before.

kpis.name: Repeat purchase rate
kpis.definition: Share of customers who placed two or more orders in the period.

benchmark.note: Indicative for consumer brands over a 12-month window; short windows read lower.

pitfalls: Depends on window length: a one-month view always looks lower than a one-year view.

kpis.name: Purchase frequency
kpis.definition: Average orders per customer in the period.

kpis.name: Customer LTV (historical)
kpis.definition: Net revenue per customer over the selected period. Historical, not a prediction.
pitfalls: Recent customers have had less time to buy again; historical LTV understates them (survivorship).

kpis.name: Days between orders
kpis.definition: Average gap between consecutive orders of repeat customers.
kpis.formula: Σ (last − first order date) ÷ Σ (orders − 1), over customers with 2+ orders
pitfalls: Pooled average of all gaps; customers with many orders weigh more than one-time repeaters.

kpis.name: Ad spend
kpis.definition: Total advertising spend.

kpis.name: Attributed revenue
kpis.definition: Revenue the ad platforms attribute to campaigns.
pitfalls: Platforms each claim credit for the same sale; attributed revenue across platforms over-counts.

kpis.name: ROAS
kpis.definition: Revenue generated per unit of ad spend.

kpis.name: Click-through rate
kpis.definition: Share of impressions that led to a click.

benchmark.note: Display and social ads typically see 0.5–3%.

kpis.name: Cost per click
kpis.definition: Average spend per click.

kpis.name: Cost per purchase
kpis.definition: Ad spend per attributed purchase.

kpis.name: Sessions
kpis.definition: Visits to the store.

kpis.name: Add-to-carts
kpis.definition: Sessions or events that added an item to cart.

kpis.name: Checkouts
kpis.definition: Checkouts started.

kpis.name: Purchases
kpis.definition: Completed purchases.

kpis.name: Conversion rate
kpis.definition: Share of sessions that ended in a purchase.

kpis.name: Add-to-cart rate
kpis.definition: Share of sessions that added to cart.

kpis.name: Cart-to-checkout rate
kpis.definition: Share of add-to-carts that started checkout.

kpis.name: Checkout completion
kpis.definition: Share of checkouts that became purchases.

kpis.name: Stock on hand
kpis.definition: Units in stock at the latest snapshot in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of stock on the latest snapshot date (semi-additive)

variants.label: Single snapshot
variants.caveat: No snapshot date, so the file is treated as one point-in-time snapshot.

pitfalls: Stock is semi-additive: add across SKUs, never across dates.

kpis.name: Active SKUs
kpis.definition: SKUs present in the latest snapshot.
kpis.formula: Distinct SKUs on the latest snapshot date

kpis.name: Stock-out rate
kpis.definition: Share of SKUs with no stock at the latest snapshot.

kpis.name: SKUs below reorder level
kpis.definition: SKUs at or under their reorder point (stock-out risk).
kpis.formula: Distinct SKUs where stock ≤ reorder level (latest snapshot)

kpis.name: Sell-through rate
kpis.definition: Share of available units that sold in the period.
pitfalls: Approximates opening stock + receipts as sold + closing stock.

kpis.name: Days of cover
kpis.definition: How many days current stock lasts at the period's average daily sales.

kpis.name: Inventory turnover
kpis.definition: How many times average inventory value was sold through in the period.
kpis.formula: COGS (units sold × unit cost) ÷ average inventory value across snapshots

kpis.name: Orders per customer
kpis.definition: Lifetime orders per customer.

kpis.name: Repeat customer share
kpis.definition: Share of customers with two or more lifetime orders.

kpis.name: Average lifetime spend
kpis.definition: Lifetime spend per customer.

kpis.name: Products
kpis.definition: Distinct SKUs in the catalogue.

kpis.name: Average list price
kpis.definition: Simple average selling price across catalogue SKUs.
kpis.formula: Average of unit price over SKUs

kpis.name: Catalogue margin %
kpis.definition: Price-weighted margin across SKUs that have a cost.
kpis.formula: Σ (price − cost) ÷ Σ price, over SKUs with a cost

charts.title: Net revenue over time
charts.reason: One measure over a continuous time axis reads best as a line; the soft fill emphasises volume without hiding the shape.

charts.title: Average order value
charts.reason: AOV is a ratio, so it is plotted as a line of the recomputed ratio per period, never summed.

charts.title: Orders over time
charts.reason: Order counts per period are discrete totals, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: New vs returning customers
charts.reason: Two parts of one whole per month: stacked columns show both the total and the mix.

charts.title: Net revenue by category
charts.reason: Comparing one measure across named categories: sorted horizontal bars keep long labels readable. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Net revenue by state
charts.reason: State-level values on a tile map keep geography recognisable without letting large states dominate the ink.

charts.title: Orders by payment method
charts.reason: Part-to-whole with six or fewer methods: a donut shows the split at a glance.

charts.title: Net revenue by channel
charts.reason: A handful of channels compared on one measure: sorted bars.

charts.title: Category and sub-category mix
charts.reason: A two-level hierarchy of contributions: a treemap shows both levels in one view.

charts.title: RTO rate by payment method
charts.reason: A rate compared across a few groups: bars of the recomputed rate per group (methods with under 30 rows are hidden as too small).

charts.title: RTO rate by state
charts.reason: Where returns-to-origin concentrate: the 12 highest-RTO states with at least 50 orders, sorted.

charts.title: Return rate by category
charts.reason: Which categories drive returns: the recomputed return rate per category, sorted, small groups hidden.

charts.title: When customers order
charts.reason: Two time dimensions and one measure: a heatmap of weekday × hour reveals daily and weekly rhythm.

charts.title: RTO rate by courier
charts.reason: Courier performance on one rate: sorted bars, couriers with under 30 orders hidden.

charts.title: Delivery days by courier
charts.reason: Average delivery time per courier, sorted; lower is better.

charts.title: Monthly cohort retention
charts.reason: Retention by acquisition month needs two time axes (cohort × months since first order): a retention heatmap.

charts.title: RFM customer segments
charts.reason: Segments as parts of the customer base, sized by customers and shaded by revenue share.

charts.title: Product concentration (Pareto)
charts.reason: How concentrated revenue is: each product's share as columns and the cumulative share as a line on the same 0–100% axis.

charts.title: Frequently bought together
charts.reason: Product pairs are a ranked list with several stats (orders together, confidence, lift), so a table is clearer than a chart.

charts.title: Units by price band
charts.reason: A measure across ordered numeric bands: columns in band order show where volume sits.

charts.title: Return rate by discount depth
charts.reason: Do deeper discounts bring lower-quality orders? The return rate per discount band, in band order.

charts.title: Return reasons
charts.reason: Counts by reason, sorted, so the biggest fixable cause is first.

charts.title: Top products
charts.reason: Several measures per product: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Ad spend over time
charts.reason: Spend over a continuous time axis.

charts.title: ROAS over time
charts.reason: A ratio over time, recomputed per period.

charts.title: ROAS by campaign
charts.reason: Campaigns compared on efficiency, sorted.

charts.title: Spend by campaign
charts.reason: Where the budget goes, sorted.

charts.title: Spend vs attributed revenue by campaign
charts.reason: Two measures per campaign: a scatter with a trendline shows which campaigns over- or under-deliver for their spend.

charts.title: Conversion funnel
charts.reason: Sequential stages with drop-off: a funnel shows stage size and loss between steps.

charts.title: Conversion rate over time
charts.reason: A rate over time, recomputed per period.

charts.title: Stock on hand by category
charts.reason: Closing stock (latest snapshot, never summed over dates) compared across categories.

charts.title: Stock-out rate by category
charts.reason: Where availability is weakest, sorted.

charts.title: Stock on hand over time
charts.reason: Closing stock per period (the latest snapshot in each period).

charts.title: Customers by state
charts.reason: Customer base by state on a tile map.

charts.title: Lifetime spend distribution
charts.reason: How spend is distributed across customers: a histogram.

charts.title: SKUs by category
charts.reason: Catalogue breadth per category, sorted.

charts.title: Price distribution
charts.reason: How SKUs spread across price points: a histogram.

pitfalls: GMV is not revenue: cancelled, returned and RTO orders inflate it.
Ratios (AOV, return rate, RTO rate, margin) must be recomputed from totals for every period and segment, never summed or averaged across rows.
Order-line data repeats the order on every line: count orders with DISTINCT, never by counting rows.
Recent periods understate returns and RTO because orders are still in transit.
New-customer counts depend on how far back the file goes: customers whose first order predates the file look new.
